techniques.name: Phishing
techniques.description: Adversary sent a spearphishing email with a macro-enabled document attachment to gain initial access. The email spoofed a legitimate finance vendor and used urgency language to compel the user to open the attachment.

techniques.name: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Specifically a spearphishing email with a malicious Office document attachment. The document required macro enablement which triggered the attack chain.

techniques.name: Malicious File Execution
techniques.description: The end user opened the malicious Word document and clicked 'Enable Content', directly executing the embedded VBA macro payload.

techniques.name: PowerShell
techniques.description: The VBA macro invoked PowerShell with an encoded command using -EncodedCommand and -WindowStyle Hidden flags to download and execute the second-stage payload while evading user visibility.

techniques.name: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.description: Malware established persistence by writing to HKCU\Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Run registry key with a disguised entry named 'AdobeUpdater'.

techniques.name: Dynamic-link Library Injection
techniques.description: Emotet loader injected malicious DLL into svchost.exe process memory to mask its network activity as legitimate Windows system traffic.

techniques.name: LSASS Memory
techniques.description: Malware accessed LSASS process memory to extract NTLM credential hashes and Kerberos ticket data for use in lateral movement.

techniques.name: Steal Web Session Cookie
techniques.description: The malware accessed Chrome and Microsoft Edge profile directories to steal browser session cookies enabling account takeover without knowing the user's password.

techniques.name: Web Protocols
techniques.description: C2 communications disguised as HTTPS web traffic to attacker-controlled domains. Traffic pattern uses custom binary protocol over port 443 to evade DPI inspection.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.description: Harvested credentials, browser cookies, and file system content were compressed and scheduled for exfiltration through the established C2 channel to 185.220.101.47:443.
